_about: The valley's biome brief as data (Claude E, lane E, 21 Oct): what the shared kit needs to paint the home valley, written before the kit exists (rules-system.md 2 and 4, 'Adding a biome'; to-all-kit-freeze). One biome with four variants: meadow (the hay slope, the open grass between places), farmland (the halt farm's fields and hedges), riverside (the Sleepwater's banks, the millpond, the orchard) and town_edge (Crossroads, the park, the cottage plots). Every family is a house ramp (art/house-palette.json); tone numbers are steps on a ramp (0 darkest, 5 lightest). Shares are of walkable ground unless named otherwise. The woodland (Claude A's golden screen) sets the kit's rules; this brief names where the valley differs from it. 'kit' is pinned when kit v1 (woodland@1) exists. Data only: nothing here paints.

used_by.woodland: claude-a (the golden screen's open ground, if it wants the meadow's turf)
used_by.brackens: claude-f (the valley side of the heath blend, moor.json's transition)
used_by.fernhollow: claude-h (the Fern hills' clearings, if any)
used_by.the land between: claude-g (the Lull plain's pastures, variant farmland)

references: Compare at the same character height with Eastward's grass and village screens (edges and the soft grid: Eastward only, Matt 21 Oct 09:23); the density and cleanliness of the golden screen (to-all-density, to-all-volume). No screenshots of other games in the repository.

palette_intent._about: The valley is the warmest green on the map and the calmest ground: one body tone per field with broad soft blotches of a sibling, flowers in clumps of a colour, never speckle (rules-system 'calm', to-all-volume 4). Warmer and yellower than the coast's sea turf, greener and wetter than the moor, lighter than the woodland floor.

hay.note: uncut hay on the slope above the garden: warm green going golden in drifts, seed heads a tone up in clumps on the lit side

pasture.note: grazed turf at the halt and the Headland's neck: cooler and shorter, darker blotches where it is wet

lawn.note: the park and the green: one even tone, mown stripes only as two broad bands a tone apart

crop.note: wheat and barley in rows along x (the grid), the margin a strip of turf with poppies (berry_warm) and cornflowers in clumps

plough.note: furrows along x every 4 texels, lit tops, no lone pixels

bank.note: the meadow edge set's earth faces between tiers, roots and rounded cobbles at the foot

lane.note: beaten earth lanes with a grass crown down the middle, wheel ruts a tone down

setts.note: Crossroads' square and the quay's approach: setts in courses along x, worn paler where feet go

drystone.note: field walls, the garden's terrace wall, the Headland's wall: rounded stones in courses with a coping of uprights

thatch_and_slate.note: valley roofs: thatch on the farm and the mill, slate in Crossroads and Driftwood (house kits)

timber_works.note: gates, stiles, the mill wheel, fences and benches: warm timber, silvered (timber_cool) only at the coast

render.note: cottage walls: limewash, warm in the village, a tone down on the north sides

stream.note: the brook and the river: clear brown-green over gravel near the banks, sky_cool glints sparse and clumped where light catches

pond.note: the millpond and the dew pond: still, darkest under the bank, reflections of the bank trees a tone down

ground._about: Ground recipes by kind: a body family, one or two siblings in broad soft blotches (2 to 3 tones apart at most), and dressing in clumps placed by rule (every 16 to 32 world px at bases, Claude B's prop_clusters dressing). Despeckle after every pass; no lone pixels.

plants.where: singly in the hay meadow and the park, in hedgerows every 4 to 6 cells
plants.note: broad crown in lit lumps, top-left bright, a dark core; the old oak on the coastal lowland the largest

plants.where: hedgerows and the Fern hills' foot
plants.note: lighter, airier crown than oak; never in a row with another ash
leaning over the water, pollards in a row along the race

plants.where: the orchard in rows, cottage gardens singly
plants.note: fruit in clumps on the lit side, blossom in spring

plants.where: field boundaries along x and y, gaps only at gates and stiles
plants.note: three or more shrubs mixed in any run (benchmark 9): hawthorn, hazel, holly, a standard oak

plants.where: lane verges and the hedge foot in drifts
pasture and hay in small rings
the millpond's west end, the river's slack water
the hedge foot on north sides and the escarpment's foot

tiers.notes: tiers 3 to 7 in the valley (Claude G's world tiers): masses step in and out by whole cells, at least 16 px, every screen width or so (to-all-volume 1); outlines on the cell grid with rounded corners (eastward-edges 1.6), square only on built edges (the garden's terrace wall, the quay); the escarpment over the woodland is the only 64 px face.

meadow.where: turf banks between the valley's tiers
meadow.shapes: an earth face with roots and rounded cobbles in it, a sod lip overhanging by a texel or two with grass falling over the edge, cobbles and a grass fringe at the foot (to-all-volume 3)

terrace_wall.where: the garden's south wall over the square, the mill's step, retaining walls behind Crossroads' north side
terrace_wall.shapes: drystone courses of rounded stones, a coping of uprights, ivy in clumps from the top; square corners

hedge_bank.shapes: a low earth bank a cell high under the hedge, the hedge's shadow down-right on the field

stream_bank.where: the brook, the race and the river
stream_bank.shapes: a cut bank (earth, roots, a dark undercut) on the outside of a turn and a gravel bar on the inside, reeds in clumps, never an even ribbon

pond_margin.where: the millpond and the dew pond
pond_margin.shapes: a dark wet ring a texel wide, marginals in clumps, a stone or timber edge where people use it (the millpond bench, the sluice)

variants._about: Not separate biomes: the same families and edge sets with their own ground mix and plants.

meadow.where: the hay slope above the garden, the Headland's neck inside the wall, the open grass between places

farmland.where: the halt farm: the farmyard, four field blocks drained to the windmill, the fields down to the shingle

riverside.where: the millpond and the mill, the orchard, the miller's cottage, the Sleepwater from the mill to the estuary, the park's bank

town_edge.where: Crossroads (the square, the green, the cottage plots), the park, the top of Driftwood above the quay

water.stream: the brook and the river run on the grid (along x or y, turning at cell corners), a constant width through each run, widening at the estuary; detail_bar's 'stream' kind
water.falls: the Sleepwater's escarpment fall (Claude A's woodland), the mill's wheel at the terrace step, a low fall where the floor steps down to the lowland: the cliff core's neutral fall, white for a cell, then calm
water.still: the millpond and the dew pond: still water (water_flow's still mask), reflections only
water.motion: flow frames move a pixel one tone along its own ramp (never a new colour); finite and off when the screen is inactive or motion is reduced

proposed.millpond_bench: a bench at the pond's lit edge facing the water, a willow behind it, a rod rest (the angler's rest spot)
proposed.green_shelter: the shelter by the green: a bench under a roof on posts, a hook on the post (the gardener's story reserves a kettle, a trowel and a lantern there), a noticeboard
proposed.cottage_front: a cottage door with a bench beside it, a tub of flowers, a water butt at the corner, washing on a line behind
proposed.well_square: the square well with its bucket, a bench facing it, pigeons, a lamp at the nearest corner

day: the mill wheel's turn and splash
the train's whistle from the halt, now and then
night: lit windows in Crossroads as the warm points
ambience.light: upper-left sun; cast shadows two tones down on grass, one on water; the valley is the brightest, warmest screen at noon

transitions._about: This biome's side of each meeting, for Claude G's scripts/art/biomes/transitions.json: a shared middle terrain both sides blend into over a band of 64 to 160 px, or a built seam.

forest.middle: wood_edge: meadow under scattered oaks and hazel, bracken and foxglove thickening into the woodland's floor
forest.where: the woodland's east and south edges (claude-a), the Fern hills (claude-h)

highland.middle: the hay meadow thinning into short turf with scree and boulders at the escarpment's foot

moor.middle: heath: heather drifts break into tufts, then turf with tormentil (river_kit.heath's idea)
moor.where: the Brackens' foot west of the halt (claude-f)

coast.middle: sea turf: meadow cooling and shortening over 160 px, clover giving way to thrift; at the halt, fields into shingle
coast.where: Driftwood, the Headland, the halt farm's shore (claude-e, coast.json cliff_coast)

steppe.middle: pasture yellowing into the steppe's turf (dry_kit's steppe band)
steppe.where: the Drover's Road and the Ash Coast leaving west (claude-d, claude-g)

city.edge: the village's setts end at a lane of beaten earth; no city faces in the valley

river.middle: the riverside variant is the river's own bank in the valley
river.where: the Sleepwater (claude-e); the Lull's plain (claude-g, claude-i) takes farmland and riverside

port_from: river_kit.py (#133, on main): river, ford, stepping_stones, riffles, race, reeds and marginals, bank trees, meadow, pasture, fields with margins, hedgerows with gates, blend, heath, wood_edge; forest_kit.py (#155, frozen): tree crowns and undergrowth, the wooded bank. Their techniques are graded and ported by Claude A's side (to-all-kit-freeze); this brief does not extend them.
